title: ElevenLabs Voice Changer for Creators: A Practical Starting Guide
markdown:
ElevenLabs Voice Changer is worth considering when you already have a recording and want to transform it into a different selected or custom voice. The official workflow is straightforward: upload an audio file or record in the app, select a voice and settings, generate the result, then download it or bring it into Studio. [ElevenLabs Voice Changer](https://elevenlabs.io/voice-changer)

The product page says the service can preserve elements such as emotion, cadence, accents, and subtle vocal traits during voice transformation. It also describes a library of more than 10,000 voices, the ability to design a new voice, background-noise removal, and use in Studio. These are capabilities to evaluate against your own source audio and creative requirements—not promises that every recording will produce a particular result. [ElevenLabs Voice Changer](https://elevenlabs.io/voice-changer)

For planning usage, ElevenLabs lists Voice Changer at approximately 1,000 credits per minute, with credits shared across its products. Its public monthly plans list Free at $0 with 10,000 credits, Starter at $6 with 30,000 credits, Creator at $22 with 121,000 credits (the page also notes a first-month $11 offer), and Pro at $99 with 600,000 credits; taxes, levies, and duties are excluded. Check the current plan details and credit allocation before committing, especially if you also use other ElevenLabs tools. [ElevenLabs pricing](https://elevenlabs.io/pricing)

A sensible decision checklist is: confirm that uploading or recording suits your workflow, audition voices that match the role you need, estimate minutes from the shared credit pool, and review any licensing or team requirements for the plan under consideration. ElevenLabs also states that the web interface accepts common audio formats including MP3, WAV, and AAC, and offers API and SDK access for programmatic voice transformation. [ElevenLabs Voice Changer](https://elevenlabs.io/voice-changer)
